#!/bin/bash
# Build a UEFI-bootable disk image with GRUB2 for TychaiOS
set -e

LINUX_SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
OUT="$LINUX_SRC/esp.img"
MNT="/tmp/tychain_esp"

BZIMAGE="$LINUX_SRC/arch/x86/boot/bzImage"
INITRAMFS="$LINUX_SRC/initramfs.cpio.gz"

# ---------- sanity checks ----------
[ -f "$BZIMAGE" ]   || { echo "ERROR: bzImage not found at $BZIMAGE"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$INITRAMFS" ] || { echo "ERROR: initramfs not found at $INITRAMFS"; exit 1; }

command -v grub2-mkstandalone >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "Installing grub2-efi tools..."; sudo zypper -n install grub2-x86_64-efi; }

# ---------- embed grub.cfg into standalone EFI binary ----------
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$TMPDIR/grub.cfg" << 'EOF'
set default=0
set timeout=3

menuentry "TychaiOS" {
    linux /boot/bzImage console=tty1 rdinit=/init
    initrd /boot/initramfs.cpio.gz
}
EOF

echo "Building standalone GRUB EFI binary..."
grub2-mkstandalone \
    --format=x86_64-efi \
    --output="$TMPDIR/BOOTX64.EFI" \
    "boot/grub/grub.cfg=$TMPDIR/grub.cfg"

# ---------- create FAT32 ESP image (128 MB) ----------
echo "Creating ESP disk image..."
dd if=/dev/zero of="$OUT" bs=1M count=128 status=none

# partition: GPT with one EFI partition
sgdisk -Z "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
sgdisk --new=1:2048:+120M --typecode=1:EF00 --change-name=1:"EFI System" "$OUT" >/dev/null

# format the partition (use a loop device so mkfs.fat targets the partition)
LOOP=$(sudo losetup --find --show --partscan "$OUT")
sudo mkfs.fat -F 32 -n "EFI" "${LOOP}p1" >/dev/null

# mount and populate
sudo mkdir -p "$MNT"
sudo mount "${LOOP}p1" "$MNT"

sudo mkdir -p "$MNT/EFI/BOOT"
sudo mkdir -p "$MNT/boot"
sudo cp "$TMPDIR/BOOTX64.EFI" "$MNT/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI"
sudo cp "$BZIMAGE"             "$MNT/boot/bzImage"
sudo cp "$INITRAMFS"           "$MNT/boot/initramfs.cpio.gz"

sudo umount "$MNT"
sudo losetup -d "$LOOP"
rm -rf "$TMPDIR"

echo ""
echo "Done: $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1))"
echo ""
echo "Boot command (Windows QEMU):"
echo "  qemu-system-x86_64.exe \\"
echo "    -drive file=$(wslpath -w "$OUT"),format=raw \\"
echo "    -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=...\ovmf\code.bin \\"
echo "    -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=...\ovmf\vars.bin \\"
echo "    -m 512M -smp 2 -vga std"

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Build a UEFI-bootable GPT disk image with GRUB2 — no sudo required
set -e

LINUX_SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
DISK="$LINUX_SRC/esp.img"
BZIMAGE="$LINUX_SRC/arch/x86/boot/bzImage"
INITRAMFS="$LINUX_SRC/initramfs.cpio.gz"

[ -f "$BZIMAGE" ]   || { echo "ERROR: bzImage missing at $BZIMAGE"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$INITRAMFS" ] || { echo "ERROR: initramfs missing at $INITRAMFS"; exit 1; }

# Install tools if missing
for pkg_check in "grub2-mkstandalone:grub2-x86_64-efi" "sgdisk:gptfdisk" "mformat:mtools"; do
    cmd="${pkg_check%%:*}"; pkg="${pkg_check##*:}"
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Installing $pkg..."; sudo zypper -n install "$pkg"; }
done

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $TMPDIR" EXIT

# ── 1. grub.cfg embedded in the standalone EFI binary ──────────────────────
cat > "$TMPDIR/grub.cfg" << 'GRUBCFG'
set default=0
set timeout=3

menuentry "TychaiOS" {
    linux  /boot/bzImage console=tty1 rdinit=/init
    initrd /boot/initramfs.cpio.gz
}
GRUBCFG

echo "Building standalone GRUB EFI binary..."
grub2-mkstandalone \
    --format=x86_64-efi \
    --output="$TMPDIR/BOOTX64.EFI" \
    "boot/grub/grub.cfg=$TMPDIR/grub.cfg"

# ── 2. Create FAT32 partition image (no loop device / no sudo) ──────────────
# EFI partition: 128 MB, starts at sector 2048 (1 MiB offset)
FAT_SECTORS=262144   # 128 MiB in 512-byte sectors
FAT_IMG="$TMPDIR/fat.img"

echo "Formatting FAT32 partition image..."
dd if=/dev/zero of="$FAT_IMG" bs=512 count=$FAT_SECTORS status=none
mkdosfs -F 32 -n "EFI" "$FAT_IMG" >/dev/null

echo "Populating EFI partition..."
mmd  -i "$FAT_IMG" ::EFI
mmd  -i "$FAT_IMG" ::EFI/BOOT
mmd  -i "$FAT_IMG" ::boot
mcopy -i "$FAT_IMG" "$TMPDIR/BOOTX64.EFI"  ::EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI
mcopy -i "$FAT_IMG" "$BZIMAGE"              ::boot/bzImage
mcopy -i "$FAT_IMG" "$INITRAMFS"            ::boot/initramfs.cpio.gz

# ── 3. Assemble GPT disk image ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Total size: 1 MiB gap + 128 MiB partition + 1 MiB GPT backup = 130 MiB
DISK_MB=130
echo "Creating GPT disk image (${DISK_MB} MiB)..."
dd if=/dev/zero of="$DISK" bs=1M count=$DISK_MB status=none

# Write GPT: one EFI partition, sector 2048 to 2048+FAT_SECTORS-1
sgdisk \
    --new=1:2048:$((2048 + FAT_SECTORS - 1)) \
    --typecode=1:EF00 \
    --change-name=1:"EFI System" \
    "$DISK" >/dev/null

# Embed the FAT32 image at the partition offset (sector 2048 = 1 MiB)
dd if="$FAT_IMG" of="$DISK" bs=512 seek=2048 conv=notrunc status=none

echo ""
echo "Done: $DISK ($(du -h "$DISK" | cut -f1))"

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Copy and decompress bochs DRM module into rootfs for /dev/fb0
set -e

LINUX_SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
ROOTFS="$LINUX_SRC/rootfs"
MODDIR="$ROOTFS/lib/modules"

KVER=$(ls /lib/modules/ | grep -v microsoft | sort -V | tail -1)

copy_mod() {
    local src="$1" name="$2"
    local zst="/lib/modules/$KVER/$src.ko.zst"
    local plain="/lib/modules/$KVER/$src.ko"
    if [ -f "$zst" ]; then
        zstd -d "$zst" -o "$MODDIR/$name.ko" --force -q
        echo "  $name.ko (decompressed from $KVER)"
    elif [ -f "$plain" ]; then
        cp "$plain" "$MODDIR/$name.ko"
        echo "  $name.ko (from $KVER)"
    else
        echo "  WARNING: $name not found in /lib/modules/$KVER"
        return 1
    fi
}

mkdir -p "$MODDIR"

# bochs DRM: claims Bochs VBE PCI device, creates /dev/dri/card0
# ttm: memory manager that bochs may need (load first just in case)
copy_mod "kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/ttm/ttm"         "ttm"   || true
copy_mod "kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/tiny/bochs"       "bochs"

ls -lh "$MODDIR/"

arguments.content:
# TychaiOS

A minimal custom OS built on the Linux 3.0.1 kernel source tree with a fully custom userland. No systemd, no glibc in the rootfs, no bash — just static binaries and a hand-rolled init.

> **Name origin:** From the Greek *tychaíos* (τυχαίος) meaning "random" — and stylised as *TychaiOS* because it sounds like a legitimate OS name.

---

## Identity

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| OS name | TychaiOS |
| Default user | `angel` |
| Hostname | `heaven` |
| Shell | `busybox sh` (static) |
| Init | `minit` (custom PID 1) |
| Kernel | openSUSE 7.0.6 bzImage (boot) / Linux 3.0.1 (source, long-term target) |

---

## Directory Structure

```
linux-3.0.1/
├── arch/x86/boot/bzImage    # kernel image (openSUSE 7.0.6, used for testing)
├── initramfs.cpio.gz        # packed root filesystem
├── esp.img                  # GRUB EFI disk image (for UEFI boot)
├── ovmf/
│   ├── code.bin             # OVMF UEFI firmware (read-only)
│   └── vars.bin             # OVMF variable store
├── rootfs/                  # the actual root filesystem
│   ├── init                 # PID 1 (minit)
│   ├── bin/
│   │   ├── sh               # busybox static
│   │   ├── sysinfo          # system info display
│   │   ├── snake            # TUI snake game
│   │   ├── snake-fb         # framebuffer snake game
│   │   ├── calc             # interactive calculator
│   │   ├── shutdown         # power off
│   │   ├── reboot           # reboot
│   │   └── minit            # minitctl (minit frontend)
│   ├── lib/modules/
│   │   ├── bochs.ko         # Bochs VBE DRM driver (for /dev/fb0)
│   │   └── ttm.ko           # DRM TTM memory manager
│   └── etc/
│       └── profile          # environment, aliases, module loading, sysinfo
├── minit/                   # PID 1 source
├── userland/
│   ├── sysinfo/             # sysinfo source
│   ├── snake/               # TUI snake source
│   ├── snake_fb/            # framebuffer snake source
│   ├── calc/                # calculator source
│   ├── power/               # shutdown/reboot source
│   └── minitctl/            # minit control frontend source
├── tools/
│   ├── setup-gcc45.sh       # builds GCC 4.5.0 from source (for kernel 3.0.1)
│   ├── setup-bochs-module.sh# copies + decompresses bochs/ttm kernel modules
│   ├── make-grub-disk.sh    # builds GRUB EFI disk image (esp.img)
│   ├── check-fb-config.sh   # checks framebuffer kernel config
│   └── find-ovmf.sh         # locates OVMF firmware files
├── GNUmakefile              # project build system (takes priority over kernel Makefile)
└── build.sh                 # legacy full build script
```

---

## Userland Components

All binaries are compiled as **fully static** with `clang -static`. No shared libraries in the rootfs.

### `minit` — PID 1
Custom init process. Never exits. Responsibilities:
- Mounts `devtmpfs` on `/dev`, `proc` on `/proc`, `sysfs` on `/sys`
- Spawns `/bin/sh --login` on the console
- Reaps orphan processes (`waitpid` loop)
- Handles signals via `signalfd`
- Unix socket IPC at `/run/minit.sock` for `minitctl`

Environment set by minit: `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER=angel`, `LOGNAME=angel`, `TERM=linux`, `SHELL`.

### `sysinfo` — system info display
Runs automatically on login (via `/etc/profile`). Displays:
```
angel@heaven
────────────
OS:     TychaiOS
Kernel: kernel 7.0.6-1-default
...
```
Uses ANSI colours (cyan/bold). Reads hostname via `gethostname()`, user via `getenv("USER")`.

### `snake` — TUI snake game
Terminal snake game using ANSI escape codes. Runs in any terminal. Arrow keys or WASD to move.

### `snake-fb` — framebuffer snake game
Graphical snake game that writes directly to `/dev/fb0`. Features:
- Auto-detects screen resolution via `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` / `FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO`
- Back-buffer rendering (no flicker)
- Pixel-format portable (`mkcolor()` uses `vinfo.red.offset` etc.)
- 5×7 bitmap font for score display
- Game-over screen: darkens pixels ÷3, draws centred overlay box
- Requires `/dev/fb0` — prints helpful message if unavailable

### `calc` — interactive calculator
Recursive descent expression parser. Supports:
- `+` `-` `*` `/` `%` with correct operator precedence
- Parentheses and unary minus
- Floating point (prints as integer when result is whole)
- Type `q` / `quit` / `exit` or Ctrl+D to quit

```
calc — type an expression, 'q' to quit
> 2 + 3 * 4
= 14
> (2 + 3) * 4
= 20
> 10 / 3
= 3.33333
```

### `shutdown` / `reboot` — power control
Single binary (`power`) installed as both. Uses `sync()` + `kill(-1, SIGTERM)` + `kill(-1, SIGKILL)` + `reboot(2)` syscall.

- `shutdown [-h|-p|--halt|--poweroff] now` → powers off
- `reboot` → reboots
- Flags `-r` / `--reboot` on shutdown binary also reboots

### `minitctl` — minit frontend
Communicates with minit over the Unix socket at `/run/minit.sock`. Installed as `minit` in `/bin`.

---

## `/etc/profile`

Runs on every shell login. Sets environment and loads the DRM framebuffer module:

```sh
export PATH=/bin:/sbin
export HOME=/root
export USER=angel
export LOGNAME=angel
export TERM=linux
export SHELL=/bin/sh

alias clear='printf "\033[H\033[2J"'
alias cls='printf "\033[H\033[2J"'

# Load bochs DRM so /dev/fb0 appears (QEMU -vga std, Bochs VBE PCI)
if [ ! -e /dev/fb0 ]; then
    [ -f /lib/modules/ttm.ko ]   && insmod /lib/modules/ttm.ko
    [ -f /lib/modules/bochs.ko ] && insmod /lib/modules/bochs.ko && sleep 0.5
fi

sysinfo
```

---

## Build System

The project uses `GNUmakefile` (takes precedence over the Linux kernel's `Makefile`).

```
make            # build everything: userland + modules + initramfs + disk
make userland   # compile all C binaries only
make modules    # copy bochs/ttm kernel modules into rootfs
make initramfs  # pack rootfs into initramfs.cpio.gz
make disk       # build GRUB EFI disk image (esp.img)
make run        # launch QEMU with OVMF
make clean      # remove binaries and initramfs
make distclean  # also remove esp.img and kernel modules
```

All WSL-side work runs via `wsl.exe -e /bin/bash ...` from Windows.

---

## QEMU / Boot

### Direct kernel boot (recommended, used for development)

```
"C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe" \
  -kernel D:\linux-3.0.1\arch\x86\boot\bzImage \
  -initrd D:\linux-3.0.1\initramfs.cpio.gz \
  -append "console=ttyS0 console=tty1 rdinit=/init nokaslr" \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\code.bin \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\vars.bin \
  -m 512M -smp 2 -vga std -serial stdio
```

- `-serial stdio` pipes kernel log to the terminal window
- OVMF provides UEFI firmware (required for GOP/framebuffer)
- `-vga std` presents a Bochs VBE PCI device that `bochs.ko` claims

### GRUB EFI disk boot (alternative)

```
"C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe" \
  -drive file=D:\linux-3.0.1\esp.img,format=raw,if=virtio \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\code.bin \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\vars.bin \
  -m 512M -smp 2 -vga std
```

### OVMF firmware

Sourced from openSUSE WSL (`/usr/share/qemu/ovmf-x86_64-4m-code.bin` and `...-vars.bin`), copied to `ovmf/code.bin` and `ovmf/vars.bin` for access by the Windows QEMU binary.

---

## Framebuffer (`/dev/fb0`)

The openSUSE 7.0.6 kernel has `CONFIG_DRM_BOCHS=m` (module) with `CONFIG_DRM_FBDEV_EMULATION=y`. Loading `bochs.ko` makes the Bochs VBE PCI device (presented by `-vga std`) register a DRM device, which the fbdev emulation layer exposes as `/dev/fb0`.

`bochs.ko` depends on `ttm.ko` — both are decompressed from the host kernel (`.ko.zst` → `.ko`) and included in the initramfs.

**Kernel config relevant to framebuffer:**
```
CONFIG_SYSFB=y
CONFIG_DRM_SIMPLEDRM=y       # built-in, but needs SYSFB_SIMPLEFB
CONFIG_DRM_BOCHS=m           # module, claims Bochs VBE PCI device directly
CONFIG_DRM_FBDEV_EMULATION=y # creates /dev/fb0 from DRM device
CONFIG_FB=y
CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y
```

Note: `CONFIG_SYSFB_SIMPLEFB` is **not set** in this kernel, so `simpledrm` cannot claim the EFI framebuffer. The bochs module path bypasses this limitation entirely.

---

## GCC 4.5.0 (Linux 3.0.1 kernel compilation)

The long-term goal is to compile the Linux 3.0.1 kernel with GCC 4.5.0 (era-correct compiler). GCC 4.5.0 is built from source by `tools/setup-gcc45.sh` and installed to `/usr/local/gcc-4.5/`.

Patches applied to GCC 4.5.0 source for compatibility with modern build environments:

| Patch | File | Fix |
|-------|------|-----|
| 4a | `libiberty/safe-ctype.c` | Add `#include <string.h>` |
| 4b | `gcc/reload1.c` | Set `spill_indirect_levels = 0` |
| 4d | `include/linux/compiler-gcc4_5.h` | Copy from `compiler-gcc4.h` |
| 4e | `gcc/tree.h` + gcc/ files | Rename `thread_local` bitfield → `decl_thread_local` (C11 keyword clash) |
| 4f | `gcc/config/i386/linux-unwind.h` | `struct ucontext *` → `ucontext_t *` (glibc rename) |

Build flags: `MAKEINFO=true` (skip texinfo docs), `CFLAGS_FOR_TARGET="-O1 -Wno-error -fno-strict-aliasing"` (suppress incompatible warning flags from host GCC).

---

## Known Issues / Limitations

- `/dev/fb0` requires `insmod` at login — not available before the shell starts
- `snake-fb` must be run after profile loads (modules need ~0.5s after insmod)
- GRUB EFI disk boot hangs at early kernel init (under investigation; direct boot is stable)
- Linux 3.0.1 kernel compilation not yet completed (NTFS clock skew prevented `make` from producing output; GCC 4.5.0 is ready)
- WSL `wsl -e bash -c "..."` broken due to `E:\unsloth_studio\Scripts` in Windows PATH failing translation — use script files via `wsl.exe -e /bin/bash /mnt/d/...script.sh` instead

- `all` no longer auto-builds the disk (run `make disk` explicitly when needed)
`$(shell pwd)` fails on Windows make — use `$(CURDIR)` instead, which is a GNU make builtin that needs no shell:

Also the `run-disk` prerequisite check will still fail on Windows because make tries to build `esp.img` using WSL commands. Strip the prerequisite from the launch targets so they just fire the QEMU command directly:

arguments.old_string:

	"$(QEMU)" \
arguments.new_string:

events.text: Try `make run-disk` again — `$(CURDIR)` will resolve to `D:\linux-3.0.1` without needing a shell, and the launch targets have no prerequisites that would trigger WSL builds.

The key entry across all logs is the same crash pattern:

```
IDT=0000000000000000 00000000    ← IDT is null
v=0d (General Protection Fault) at RIP=0x124a1dd
check_exception old: 0xd new 0xd → double fault
check_exception old: 0x8 new 0xd → Triple fault
```

This is **OVMF crashing internally** — not the kernel, not GRUB. OVMF switches to 64-bit long mode but has a null IDT, so the first exception immediately triple-faults. The culprit is `ovmf/vars.bin` — it accumulates EFI variable state across boots and has become corrupted from the repeated failed GRUB attempts.

Fix: reset vars.bin to a clean copy:

arguments.command: wsl.exe -e /bin/bash -c "KVER=\$(ls /lib/modules/ | grep -v microsoft | sort -V | tail -1); find /usr/share/qemu -name '*vars*' 2>/dev/null | head -5; find /usr/share/edk2* -name '*vars*' 2>/dev/null | head -5"
arguments.description: Find clean OVMF vars image to restore from

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Reset OVMF vars.bin to a clean state (fixes triple fault from corrupted EFI variables)
SRC="/usr/share/qemu/ovmf-x86_64-opensuse-4m-vars.bin"
DST="/mnt/d/linux-3.0.1/ovmf/vars.bin"
cp "$SRC" "$DST"
echo "Reset vars.bin from $SRC ($(du -h $DST | cut -f1))"

arguments.description: Reset OVMF vars.bin to clean state

events.text: `vars.bin` is now clean. Try `make run` or `make run-disk` again — OVMF should initialize without the triple fault. Also add `reset-ovmf-vars` to the GNUmakefile so you can easily do this again if vars.bin gets corrupted:

arguments.new_string:
distclean: clean
	rm -f $(DISK)
	rm -rf $(ROOTFS)/lib/modules

reset-ovmf:
	bash tools/reset-ovmf-vars.sh

arguments.old_string:
.PHONY: all userland modules initramfs disk run run-disk clean distclean \
        minit sysinfo snake snake-fb power minitctl calc
arguments.new_string:
.PHONY: all userland modules initramfs disk run run-disk clean distclean \
        minit sysinfo snake snake-fb power minitctl calc reset-ovmf

events.text: Run `make reset-ovmf` any time OVMF starts triple-faulting again — it just means the EFI variable store got into a bad state.

Two problems with that command:

1. **`append "`** between the `-initrd` and `-append` lines is a stray artifact — QEMU sees it as an unknown argument and bails or misbehaves
2. **No OVMF** — without the pflash drives the kernel can't see the EFI framebuffer, and without `-no-reboot` a kernel panic loops forever
3. **WSL QEMU + `-vga std`** tries to open a GTK window which fails silently in WSL

Use the **Windows exe from CMD/PowerShell** — that's the one that actually shows a window:

```
"C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe" -kernel D:\linux-3.0.1\arch\x86\boot\bzImage -initrd D:\linux-3.0.1\initramfs.cpio.gz -append "console=ttyS0 console=tty1 rdinit=/init nokaslr" -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\code.bin -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=D:\linux-3.0.1\ovmf\vars.bin -m 512M -smp 2 -vga std -serial stdio -no-reboot
```

Or from WSL if you really want to use the Linux binary, add `-nographic -serial stdio` and drop `-vga std` so you get output in the terminal:

```bash
qemu-system-x86_64 \
    -kernel /mnt/d/linux-3.0.1/arch/x86/boot/bzImage \
    -initrd /mnt/d/linux-3.0.1/initramfs.cpio.gz \
    -append "console=ttyS0 rdinit=/init nokaslr no-reboot" \
    -m 512M -smp 2 -nographic -serial stdio -no-reboot
```

That last one gives you a serial console in the terminal directly. No framebuffer though — `snake-fb` needs the Windows QEMU path with OVMF.

`-nographic` already maps serial to stdio automatically — `-serial stdio` is redundant and conflicts. Drop it:

```bash
qemu-system-x86_64 \
    -kernel /mnt/d/linux-3.0.1/arch/x86/boot/bzImage \
    -initrd /mnt/d/linux-3.0.1/initramfs.cpio.gz \
    -append "console=ttyS0 rdinit=/init nokaslr" \
    -m 512M -smp 2 -nographic -no-reboot
```
